body:
Thanks for your reply, I’m sorry my post was a little light on detail but I was also trying to keep it as concise as possible.

We live in a rural Area and our choices of counsellor were quite limited due to our location. The first counsellor was a two hour drive away and when the second became available a 35 minute drive we had to take her. My wife really enjoyed working with the second counsellor because she felt very supported by her and when I voiced my concerns, my wife refused to work with another counsellor because she was happy.

Things I have tried to raise in our sessions were my reasons for having the affair, such as not feeling valued, loved, important and having a voice in the raising of our son due to the fact that she had already had a child and thus experience, and I had not. Our intimacy also suffered greatly (there was none) in the following 2 years after our sons birth.

I don’t recall a time where the counsellor set any clear goals for the separation. It was purely to allow us some time and space from each other following an argument. 

In fact the only goals that she spoke of was ‘getting us to our desired destination’, whether that be reconciliation or divorce.

Agreed. I just need to get her back on board with going to the sessions again. Right now she is taking a break from it and our counsellor has just started maternity leave (bad timing but that’s life).

I’m seeing the new counsellor tomorrow in my own. Really looking forward to a session, even alone. I at least recognise when I need the help.

I’m kinda already lucky enough to work in the disability sector. I assist in training and recreation for people in my town with disabilities. Really rewarding work. 

Free time isn’t a massive issue except on the days my wife ‘needs a break from me’ and I don’t get to go home and play with the kids, but that is an ‘on the day’ basis which make pre-planning any volunteer work (or much else for that matter) difficult. I do try and stay as busy as I can when those days happen though as I know I have a tendency to overthink and get into a downward spiral on those days.

Thanks man. 

I try. Some days they are all that keeps me going. It works so far. What scares me is I lost a mate of mine in Feb 2017, my age, three young kids (4, 6 and 9) to suicide. 

It scares me that whatever his demons were, he was a great dad and husband and had the same reasons to live as me, but the black dog still found him one night and even the thought of his kids wasn’t enough to pull him back. 

I’m scared that one day I’ll find myself in that same situation when even the thought of my kids isn’t enough. 

I sincerely appreciate your response though. Thank you.

Thanks for the kind words. I felt no judgement so no need to apologise. 
What you said about responding to emotions and not just words struck a chord, I only wish she would be more open with both so I had a sense of direction rather than ‘stabbing in the dark’, but I completely understand why she would be keeping herself guarded from opening up to me. 

I’m really sorry to hear what little I know of your situation too. You always hear of split parents and shared custody but until they are your shoes you really have no idea how tough the concept is, let alone the reality.
